questions.text:
a) i. Briefly describe the structure of a RAM machine. (3 marks)
ii. Write a simple RAM program to simulate the computation of y := x + 3, assuming x = 2. (6 marks)
b) i. Define the denotational meaning of x := 2; y := x + 3. (2 marks)
ii. For b(i) above, use mathematical functions to evaluate the new state step-by-step. (5 marks)
c) Evaluate the function expression:
(λa. a * 2)(5)
i. Show the initial configuration (2 marks)
ii. Show 2–3 key transition steps, especially when the Dump is not empty. (3 marks)
iii. Final value on the stack? (2 mark)
d) i. Write a Hoare triple to verify:
{ x = 2 } y := x + 3 { y = 5 }
(3 marks)
ii. Use an appropriate inference rule to prove the triple is valid. (4 marks)

Consider the snippet:
x := 1; y := x + 2
a. Using small-step operational semantics, describe the state transitions from the initial state. (6 marks)
b. Use big-step (natural) semantics to describe the outcome in one derivation. (5 marks)
c. Briefly explain the difference between small-step and big-step semantics using layman-friendly terms. (4 marks)

Simulate the machine evaluation of the expression:
((λx. x + 1) 5)
a) List the initial configuration of the SECD machine. (3 marks)
b) Show each step of the transition until the expression is fully evaluated. (8 marks)
c) Indicate when the Dump becomes non-empty and when it is cleared. (2 marks)
d) What value is left on the stack, and what does it represent? (2 marks)

Consider the following sequence:
x := 2; y := x + 3
a. Write individual Hoare triples for each assignment. (4 marks)
b. Use the composition rule (inference rule) to prove the correctness of:
{x = 2} x := 2; y := x + 3 {y = 5}
(8 marks)
c. What does it mean for a Hoare triple to be valid? (3 marks)

Consider the loop:
Analyze the triple:
{true} while true do skip {false}
a) Is it partially correct? Explain. (5 marks)
b) Is it totally correct? Justify your answer. (5 marks)
c) Using a real-life analogy, explain the difference between partial and total correctness. (5 marks)

a. Define the denotational meaning of x := 7; y := x + 9.
b. For (a) above, use mathematical functions to evaluate the new state step-by-step.

Evaluate the function expression:
(λa. a * 3)(8)
i. Show the initial configuration
ii. Show 2–3 key transition steps, especially when the Dump is not empty.
iii. Final value on the stack?
